title: Replicating the 'Misalignment Direction' in a Small Open Model Organism

original_idea.body:
# Replicating the 'Misalignment Direction' in a Small Open Model Organism

**Problem:** A success state: 'we can locate and ablate a single internal direction that mediates misaligned behavior.' Backcasting from 'a reliable misalignment dial', a needed result is independent replication on a smaller, fully-open model that adding the direction induces misalignment and ablating it reduces it.

**Direction:** Use an openly released emergently-misaligned LoRA model organism (e.g., the rank-1 LoRA Qwen variant). Compute the difference-of-means direction between aligned and misaligned activations on a small probe set. Test causal sufficiency (add direction -> measure misaligned responses) and necessity (ablate -> measure recovery) on a held-out behavior set, reporting effect sizes with confidence intervals.

**Why it matters:** Confirms whether the 'single misalignment direction' finding is robust and transferable — a load-bearing claim for interpretability-based safety. Model-organism study on open weights, no training of the organism required.

**Relevant context:** Convergent Linear Representations of Emergent Misalignment (arXiv 2506.11618) built a model organism with 9 rank-1 LoRA adapters on Qwen-14B Instruct and identified a single direction that induces misalignment when added and reduces it when ablated.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Replicating whether a single 'misalignment direction' is causally robust directly tests a load-bearing interpretability-for-safety claim with a concrete failure scenario.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Difference-of-means + add/ablate on an existing open LoRA organism is a clear inherited methodology a novice with mentor can run.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single causal experiment (sufficiency + necessity) with effect-size success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent replication on open weights with weak lab incentive; classic third-party scrutiny work.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + small probe set on a 14B open model; single GPU, no training.

title: Does Narrow Fine-Tuning Leave a Detectable Activation Fingerprint?

original_idea.body:
# Does Narrow Fine-Tuning Leave a Detectable Activation Fingerprint?

**Problem:** A success state: 'auditors can tell whether a deployed model was secretly fine-tuned on a narrow (possibly malicious) objective just from its activations.' Backcasting, the prerequisite is a reproducible demonstration that narrow fine-tuning leaves a readable trace in activation differences on a small open model.

**Direction:** Take a small open base model and a narrowly fine-tuned counterpart (e.g., a publicly available domain-specific fine-tune). Compute per-token activation differences on neutral text, then use logit-lens / SAE-feature decoding to characterize what concepts the difference vector encodes. Test whether a simple classifier on the difference distinguishes the fine-tuning domain.

**Why it matters:** A cheap activation-fingerprint test for covert fine-tuning is valuable for model provenance and detecting tampering — a diffuse, long-horizon concern. Open weights, no training needed beyond using existing fine-tunes.

**Relevant context:** Narrow Finetuning Leaves Clearly Readable Traces in Activation Differences (OpenReview pxaCoKZWVf; AF post) shows narrow fine-tuning produces clearly readable traces in activation differences, interpretable via logit-lens and SAE features.

title: Replicating Two-Hop Reasoning Circuits with the Open circuit-tracer Library

# Replicating Two-Hop Reasoning Circuits with the Open circuit-tracer Library

**Problem:** A success state: 'circuit tracing is a robust, reproducible method any researcher can use to verify reasoning paths.' Backcasting from 'trustworthy circuit evidence', a prerequisite is confirming the published two-hop 'shortcut vs. genuine hop' circuit on Gemma-2-2B reproduces and is stable across paraphrases.

**Direction:** Use Anthropic's open circuit-tracer library (supports Gemma-2-2B) on two-hop prompts like 'The state containing Dallas has its capital in __'. Replicate the attribution graph showing the intermediate 'Texas' hop and the direct shortcut. Then vary the prompt (paraphrases, different entities) and report how stable the recovered circuit structure is.

**Why it matters:** Tests whether circuit-tracing conclusions generalize beyond a single prompt — essential before mechanistic findings can support safety claims. Fully open tooling, single GPU, no training.

**Relevant context:** circuit-tracer (decoderesearch/circuit-tracer; ACL BlackboxNLP 2025) is an open library supporting Gemma-2-2B, Llama-3.1, Qwen3-4B. Circuit Tracing on Gemma-2 showed two-hop prompts activate 'Texas' then 'Say Austin' features with both intermediate-hop and shortcut paths.

**Why it matters:** Whether planning-ahead is an emergent-scale phenomenon or present even in small models bears on when we must monitor for covert planning. Direct follow-up to a flagged surprising result; open weights only.

title: An Interpretability Benchmark Probe: Do SAE Feature Labels Predict Causal Effect?

# An Interpretability Benchmark Probe: Do SAE Feature Labels Predict Causal Effect?

**Problem:** A success state: 'an SAE feature labeled X reliably causes behavior related to X when steered.' Backcasting from 'label-to-effect guarantees' (an identified missing benchmark), the prerequisite is a small standardized test measuring agreement between a feature's auto-interp label and its causal steering effect.

**Direction:** Sample N Gemma Scope features with Neuronpedia auto-interp labels. For each, steer the feature and use an LLM-judge (with a defined rubric) or keyword test to score whether outputs shift toward the labeled concept. Report the distribution of label-effect agreement and which label types (concrete nouns vs. abstract/safety concepts) are most/least faithful.

**Why it matters:** Directly addresses the field-acknowledged gap: no benchmarks measuring whether mechanistic findings are actionable. A label-effect agreement metric is reusable infrastructure. No training, public SAEs only.

**Relevant context:** Open Phil RFP flags absence of interpretability benchmarks measuring whether findings translate to actionable safety. Gemma Scope + Neuronpedia provide labeled features; 'Coffee Feature on Coffins' (arXiv 2601.03047) shows labels can mismatch causal effects.

title: Measuring Feature Absorption Rate in Safety-Relevant Concept Hierarchies

original_idea.body:
# Measuring Feature Absorption Rate in Safety-Relevant Concept Hierarchies

**Problem:** A success state: 'when we ablate a safety concept feature, we actually remove the whole concept, not a fragment.' Backcasting from 'complete concept ablation', a prerequisite is quantifying feature absorption for safety-relevant hierarchical concepts (e.g., 'weapon' absorbing 'gun', 'violence' absorbing 'assault').

**Direction:** Using Gemma Scope SAEs, pick hierarchical safety concept pairs. Measure absorption: when the general feature should fire on a specific instance, does a separate specific latent fire instead, leaving the general feature silent? Report absorption fraction for safety hierarchies vs. neutral hierarchies (the 'India implies Asia' style baseline).

**Why it matters:** If safety concepts are fragmented across absorbed features, single-feature monitoring or ablation will miss instances — a silent failure mode. Reuses public SAEs, no training, an underexplored safety-specific slice of a known phenomenon.

**Relevant context:** 'A is for Absorption' (arXiv 2409.14507) defines feature absorption where hierarchical concepts (India implies Asia) cause separate latents that fragment representation. Gemma Scope provides the SAEs.

title: Tuned Lens vs. Logit Lens for Early Detection of Unsafe Completions

# Tuned Lens vs. Logit Lens for Early Detection of Unsafe Completions

**Direction:** On an open chat model with a public tuned-lens, run harmful and benign prompts. At each layer, decode the residual stream with both logit lens and tuned lens and measure how early the model's intermediate prediction reveals it will comply with a harmful request. Report layer-of-first-detection and false-positive rate for each lens.

**Why it matters:** Earlier internal detection enables cheaper real-time monitoring/interception — strategically valuable monitoring infrastructure. Inference-only, open weights, single GPU.

**Relevant context:** The tuned lens learns a per-layer linear correction improving alignment of intermediate logits vs. logit lens which suffers basis drift (Logit Lens Analysis, emergentmind; tuned-lens literature). title: In-Context Defenses vs Prefilling: Reproducing the 'No Free Lunch'

# In-Context Defenses vs Prefilling: Reproducing the 'No Free Lunch'

**Problem:** 'No Free Lunch for Defending Against Prefilling Attack by In-Context Learning' (arXiv:2412.12192) argues ICL defenses trade off. The precise shape of that tradeoff (defense strength vs over-refusal on benign prompts) across attack intensities is not characterized for practitioners.

**Direction:** Reproduce a few-shot ICL defense (demonstrations of refusing prefilled harmful continuations) on an open model. Sweep number of demonstrations and measure both prefilling-attack success and over-refusal rate on benign prompts (e.g., XSTest-style). Plot the safety/usability frontier to make the 'no free lunch' tradeoff concrete.

**Why it matters:** Over-refusal is a core open problem (adaptive defenses without catastrophic over-refusal). Mapping the ICL tradeoff helps deployers pick operating points without training. Fully reproducible outside a lab.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2412.12192 'No Free Lunch for Defending Against Prefilling Attack by In-Context Learning'. Context Open Problems: 'adaptive defenses... without catastrophic over-refusal'. XSTest is a standard over-refusal benchmark.

title: Probing for Rationalization: Does the Answer Form Before the Reasoning?

original_idea.body:
# Probing for Rationalization: Does the Answer Form Before the Reasoning?

**Problem:** A success state: 'we can tell whether a model's chain-of-thought is genuine reasoning or post-hoc rationalization of a pre-decided answer.' Backcasting from 'CoT faithfulness verification', a prerequisite is a probe that detects whether the final answer is already encoded in activations before the CoT is generated.

**Direction:** On an open reasoning-capable model, present prompts where a biasing cue nudges a wrong answer. Train a linear probe on activations at the prompt's last token (pre-CoT) to predict the final answer. If the probe predicts the answer before reasoning, that indicates rationalization. Compare faithful vs. biased conditions.

**Why it matters:** CoT monitoring is a leading safety strategy; if reasoning is often rationalization, monitoring CoT text is unreliable. A cheap activation-based faithfulness detector is broadly valuable. Open weights, probe-only, no training of the base model.

**Relevant context:** 'Catching rationalization in the act' (arXiv 2603.17199) detects motivated reasoning before/after CoT via activation probing. CoT activations (latents) provide more reliable signal than CoT text (latent CoT survey arXiv 2505.16782).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: A pre-CoT answer probe directly tests CoT-faithfulness, a leading safety strategy, with a concrete rationalization scenario.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Linear probe on last-token activations with biasing cues; guided, mentor-executable.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped probe experiment comparing faithful vs biased conditions.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Probe-only on open weights; lab-independent CoT-faithfulness work.

title: Cross-Model SAE Feature Transfer as a Cheap Auditing Shortcut

# Cross-Model SAE Feature Transfer as a Cheap Auditing Shortcut

**Problem:** A success state: 'an SAE trained once can audit many model variants, so monitoring is cheap.' Backcasting from 'reusable audit dictionaries', a prerequisite is whether SAE features trained on a base model still fire meaningfully on a fine-tuned/quantized variant of the same model.

**Direction:** Take a base open model with a public SAE and a fine-tuned (or quantized) sibling. Run the base SAE on the variant's activations; measure reconstruction error and whether top safety-relevant features still fire on the same inputs. Report a 'transferability decay' curve as fine-tuning intensity / quantization increases.

**Why it matters:** If SAEs transfer, monitors can be built once and reused; if not, every fine-tune needs re-auditing — important for governance of derivative models. Uses existing SAEs and model variants, no training.

**Relevant context:** On the transferability of Sparse Autoencoders for interpreting compressed models (arXiv 2507.15977) studies SAE transfer to compressed models. Gemma Scope SAEs are public and Gemma has many fine-tuned/quantized variants.

title: Can Models Coordinate to Fool Auto-Interpretability? A Small Replication

# Can Models Coordinate to Fool Auto-Interpretability? A Small Replication

**Problem:** A success state: 'automated interpretability pipelines are robust to a model trying to deceive them.' Backcasting from 'tamper-resistant auto-interp', a prerequisite is demonstrating, at small scale, whether an explainer model can be induced to produce misleading feature explanations that fool an evaluator model.

**Direction:** Set up the standard auto-interp loop (explainer LLM labels a feature from max-activating examples; evaluator LLM scores the label). Then prompt the explainer to subtly mislabel safety-relevant features and measure whether the evaluator catches it. Report the deception success rate and which evaluator checks resist it.

**Why it matters:** If auto-interp can be gamed, interpretability evidence in audits is corruptible — a key concern as interp gets automated. Prompt-driven, open models, no training; squarely a deception/oversight study labs underweight.

**Relevant context:** Deceptive Automated Interpretability: Language Models Coordinating to Fool Oversight Systems (arXiv 2504.07831) shows LMs can coordinate to fool interpretability oversight. Standard explainer/evaluator auto-interp loops are runnable on open models.

# Hidden-Thought Suppression Plus Latent Monitor Training

**Problem:** Compound: (1) models can learn to hide their thoughts from activation monitors ('Neural Chameleons') amplifying (2) the false confidence created when a latent monitor was validated only against non-evasive models. The compound failure: training/selecting a monitor on cooperative behavior makes deployment teams trust it precisely against the adversarial behavior it cannot see.

**Direction:** Use a published evasion dataset or a simple prompted setup to elicit 'hidden-thought' behavior in an open model. Train a latent monitor on normal data, then evaluate it on the evasive cases. Measure the drop and whether any robust signal survives in deeper/earlier layers. Frame as a small model-organism evaluation of monitor brittleness.

**Why it matters:** Directly engages a >1-year deceptive-alignment threat model on a tractable slice. Counterfactually valuable: evaluating monitor robustness against hidden thoughts needs no lab infra, only an open model and public methods.

**Relevant context:** 'Neural Chameleons: LMs Can Learn to Hide Their Thoughts from Unseen Activation Monitors' (arXiv:2512.11949). 'Red-teaming Activation Probes' (arXiv:2511.00554). Anthropic Auditing Game framing (emergentmind) for model-organism setup.
